english.title: Provide false / misleading information to the appropriate UK regulator of commencement of a regulated activity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[in]_
(B)_[in connection with]_

a notice given by you under paragraph 5(2) of Schedule 4 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000,

(C)_[provided information which you knew to be]_
(D)_[recklessly provided information which was]_

false or misleading in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 6(3) and (4) of Schedule 4 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
in / in connection with a notice given by you under
para 5(2) of Sch 4 Financial Services and Markets Act 2000
provided information which you knew to be false / misleading OR
recklessly provided information which was false / misleading
in a material particular

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
